summary.en: Use pointer gaps, shared speeds and sorted order to solve common list problems.
summary.bn: পয়েন্টারের ব্যবধান, চলার গতি আর সাজানো ক্রম কাজে লাগিয়ে লিস্টের সমস্যা সমাধান করো।

notes: These implementations use C17. Compound literals and declarations in loop headers date from C99; C17 does not add automatic memory management.

examples.title: Detect a cycle by node identity
examples.explanationHtml: slow moves one link and fast moves two. Equal pointers after moving prove a cycle; equal stored marks alone would prove nothing.

examples.title: Find the middle and second node from the end
examples.explanationHtml: For four nodes, middle returns the third node. A two-link lead places slow at the second node from the end when fast reaches NULL.

examples.title: Merge two disjoint sorted chains
examples.explanationHtml: The dummy node simplifies attaching the next smallest node. Both original chains transfer ownership to the merged chain, which is freed once.

examples.title: Remove adjacent duplicates from sorted input
examples.explanationHtml: After deleting one duplicate, cur stays in place to catch a third equal value. This algorithm needs sorted input to group duplicates.

examples.title: Distinguish duplicate values from a cycle
examples.explanationHtml: Three equal marks live in three different nodes. The chain still ends at NULL, so Floyd correctly reports no cycle.

practice.title: Select the second middle
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and values (-99..99). Print Middle: value, or Middle: empty. For even n choose the later middle.
hints: Move slow once for every two fast moves.

practice.title: Get the nth node from the end
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), n values (-99..99), then k (1..17). Print Result: value or Result: absent.
hints: The lead pointer must move k links before the paired walk.

practice.title: Detect a deliberately connected cycle
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), values (-99..99), then entry (-1 for none, otherwise 0..n-1). Print Cycle: 0 or 1 and safely release all nodes.
hints: Restore the original tail link before ordinary destruction.

practice.title: Keep one copy of each sorted value
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16) and n sorted values (-99..99). Remove duplicate nodes and print List:.
hints: Do not advance cur immediately after deleting its duplicate.

practice.title: Merge sorted readings without copying nodes
practice.statementHtml: Read two counts (0..16), each followed by sorted values (-99..99). Merge disjoint chains and print List:.
hints: Attach the smaller current node to a dummy-headed result.

practice.title: Merge then remove duplicates
practice.statementHtml: Read two sorted chains: count (0..16), then values (-99..99) for each. Merge them, keep one copy per value, and print List:.
hints: The merge makes equal values adjacent.

quiz.prompt: With slow and fast starting at head, which middle does the shown loop choose for four nodes?
quiz.explanation: Both move while fast and fast->next exist. Slow advances twice, reaching index two.

quiz.prompt: What proves a cycle in Floyd’s detection loop?
options: slow and fast point to the same node after moving
quiz.explanation: Distinct nodes may store equal values. Pointer identity detects the same physical node.

quiz.prompt: Why does fast need both NULL checks before two steps?
options: Either fast or its next may be absent
quiz.explanation: Reading fast->next requires fast to exist; reading its next again requires that successor to exist.

quiz.prompt: What lead is needed to find the second node from the end?
options: Advance fast two links before paired movement
quiz.explanation: When fast reaches NULL, slow remains two nodes from that end boundary.

quiz.prompt: What ownership condition does in-place merge require?
options: The two input chains are disjoint
Both heads identify the same node
The inputs share every tail node
quiz.explanation: Shared nodes could be attached twice and create cycles. Ownership transfers into one merged chain.

quiz.prompt: Why does unique_sorted stay at cur after deleting cur->next?
options: Another duplicate may now follow cur
The next distinct value is always smaller
quiz.explanation: A run of three or more equal values needs repeated checks at the same retained node.

quiz.prompt: How much auxiliary space does Floyd’s cycle detection use?
quiz.explanation: Two moving pointers suffice. The algorithm does not record every visited node.

quiz.prompt: Which middle index results from two fast steps per slow step on length four?
quiz.explanation: Rounds move (slow,fast) from (0,0) to (1,2) to (2,4). The later middle index is two.

quiz.prompt: Do equal values in distinct nodes make pointer equality true?
quiz.explanation: The integer values compare equal, but a and b are separate live objects with different addresses. The results are 1 0.

quiz.prompt: What index is second from the end in a five-node chain?
quiz.explanation: The initial two-link lead stays fixed through three paired moves. Slow ends at index three, two nodes before the end boundary.

quiz.prompt: Why must Floyd test equality after advancing at least once?
options: Head never identifies a real node
Both pointers initially equal head even in an acyclic list
Fast needs to allocate a successor
quiz.explanation: An initial equality contains no evidence of a repeated route. A meeting after movement does.

quiz.prompt: When fast is exactly n links ahead and then reaches NULL, what does slow identify?
options: The nth node from the front always
The final node for every n
The nth node from the end
quiz.explanation: The fixed lead measures distance to the end boundary, using one-based end positions.

quiz.prompt: What input violates the ownership requirement for in-place sorted merge?
options: Two heads whose chains share a suffix
One chain longer than the other
quiz.explanation: Shared allocations could be selected through both cursors. Equal values alone are safe when nodes are disjoint.

quiz.prompt: What remains after adjacent-only duplicate removal on unsorted [7,8,7]?
quiz.explanation: Neither neighboring pair is equal. The method needs sorted input to group every duplicate run.

keyPoints.en: Slow and fast pointers select the later middle in an even-length chain.
keyPoints.bn: Slow-fast পদ্ধতির এই নিয়মে জোড় দৈর্ঘ্যে পরের middle নোডটি পাওয়া যায়।

keyPoints.en: Floyd compares node addresses after moving, never only their stored values.
keyPoints.bn: Floyd-এ চলার পরে নোডের অ্যাড্রেস তুলনা করো, শুধু মান নয়।

keyPoints.en: A fixed lead of k links finds the kth node from the end.
keyPoints.bn: দুই পয়েন্টারের ব্যবধান k লিংক রাখলে শেষ থেকে k-তম নোড পাওয়া যায়।

keyPoints.en: Merging disjoint sorted lists can reuse their existing nodes.
keyPoints.bn: আলাদা সাজানো লিস্ট merge করতে পুরোনো নোডগুলোই ব্যবহার করা যায়।

keyPoints.en: Adjacent duplicate removal needs sorted input to remove every repeated value.
keyPoints.bn: পাশাপাশি duplicate মুছে সব পুনরাবৃত্ত মান সরাতে ইনপুট সাজানো থাকতে হবে।

examQuestions.question: Prove that Floyd’s two speeds eventually meet inside a cycle.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Once both pointers are inside a cycle of length L, fast gains one node per round relative to slow. Their relative offset changes by one modulo L. Within at most L rounds it becomes zero, so both identify the same node. The path before the cycle also takes linear time.

examQuestions.question: Find the later middle and second-from-end node in [12,24,36,48].
examQuestions.answerHtml: Slow/fast middle selection gives 36. A two-link lead followed by paired movement also gives 36 as the second node from the end. The results coincide here for different reasons.

examQuestions.question: Write nth_from_end using two pointers and return NULL when n is too large.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Node *fast = head;
for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (fast == NULL) {
        return NULL;
    }
    fast = fast->next;
}
Node *slow = head;
while (fast != NULL) {
    slow = slow->next;
    fast = fast->next;
}
return slow;

Require n at least one before this fragment.

examQuestions.question: Merge [1,3,5] and [2,3,6], then remove adjacent duplicates.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Merge produces [1,2,3,3,5,6]. Keeping one node from each equal run gives [1,2,3,5,6]. The removed duplicate must be unlinked and freed; every retained node belongs to the single result chain.
